{{Quote|What about the RiftMesh? All that communications hardware, and you're telling me it doesn't work?''"<br />"''The 'Mesh works, but it's slow. It can take an hour for a beacon to relay a signal. And it's not unusual for a message to pass through a thousand beacons before being picked up.|Han Solo and Omad Kaeg, discussing the RiftMesh|<ref name="Crucible">[[Crucible (novel)|''Crucible'']]</ref>}}
The '''RiftMesh''' was a communications network used in the [[Chiloon Rift/Legends|Chiloon Rift]], a resource-rich [[Nebula/Legends|nebula]] where [[Plasma/Legends|plasma]] clouds prevented regular communication technology from functioning. The [[RiftMesh Committee]], a body associated with the [[Chiloon Rift miners' support cooperative|support cooperative]] of the Chiloon Rift's [[Mining/Legends|miners]], oversaw maintenance and expansion of the RiftMesh.
 
==Description==
{{Quote|The RiftMesh is an open network&mdash;open, as in one single channel. Everybody listens, with nothing encrypted. If a message is encrypted, the beacons won't even relay it.|Omad Kaeg, on the RiftMesh|<ref name="Crucible" />}}
The RiftMesh, known informally as the 'Mesh, was a communications network operated in the [[Chiloon Rift/Legends|Chiloon Rift]], a large, resource-rich [[Nebula/Legends|nebula]]<ref name="Crucible" /> in [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]].<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> Since, the [[Plasma/Legends|plasma]] clouds of the Rift prevented standard communication systems such as [[HoloNet transceiver/Legends|HoloNet transceivers]] and [[Distress beacon/Legends|emergency transmitters]] from functioning, the RiftMesh served as the primary means of communication within the nebula.<ref name="Crucible" />
 
The RiftMesh was hosted by a network of [[repeater beacon]]s across the Chiloon Rift that could ping messages to each other. Communication via the RiftMesh functioned slowly; it could take up to an [[Standard hour/Legends|hour]] for a transmission to be submitted by one of the beacons and a message could need to pass through thousands of beacons to reach the recipient. The RiftMesh did not support encryption and functioned as one open channel.<ref name="Crucible" />
 
Individuals operating within the Chiloon Rift generally remained within areas with RiftMesh coverage, since operating beyond the RiftMesh left one without a means of summoning help in case of an emergency. [[Pilot/Legends|Pilots]] flying [[asteroid tug]]s in the nebula used the RiftMesh to coordinate their movements so that their [[Starship/Legends|vessels]] did not concentrate too closely when accessible [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]] opened up. Due to the lack of encryption, [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] active in the Rift did not use the RiftMesh to coordinate attacks.<ref name="Crucible" />
 
Responsibility for oversight of the RiftMesh was held by the [[RiftMesh Committee]], a body associated with the [[Chiloon Rift miners' support cooperative|support cooperative]] of the Chiloon Rift's [[Mining/Legends|miners]]. The RiftMesh received routine maintenance and upgrades and the RiftMesh Committee took votes on where to focus these upkeep and expansion efforts.<ref name="Crucible" />
 
==History==
{{Quote|The support cooperative gave up trying to extend the RiftMesh into the Bubble more than a hundred years ago. The beacons kept drifting out of range of each other, no matter how many the repair crews placed.|Omad Kaeg, on the miners' support cooperative's failed attempt to extend the RiftMesh to the Bubble of the Lost|<ref name="Crucible" />}}
Sometime prior to [[55 BBY/Legends|55 BBY]],<ref name="Date">[[Crucible (novel)|''Crucible'']] states that the unsuccessful attempt to expand the RiftMesh to the [[Bubble of the Lost]] occurred over one hundred [[Standard year/Legends|years]] prior to the events of the novel. Since ''Crucible'' is set in [[45 ABY]], this places the failed RiftMesh expansion effort to before [[55 BBY/Legends|55 BBY]].</ref> the Chiloon Rift miners' support cooperative unsuccessfully attempted to expand the RiftMesh into the [[Bubble of the Lost]], a region in the heart of the Chiloon Rift that surrounded a [[Unidentified monolith|monolith]] of unknown origin. The [[Space–time-warping gate|space-time-warping]] properties of the monolith caused RiftMesh repeater beacons placed in the zone to drift out of position and the effort was abandoned.
 
In [[45 ABY]], businessman [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] used the RiftMesh to ask his associate [[Omad Kaeg]]] to transport Calrissian's friends Han Solo and Leia Organa Solo from Brink Station, on the edge of the Rift, to his [[Sarnus Refinery]]. Around the same time, Mandalorian mercenaries working for [[Galactic Exploitation Technologies]] lured the [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|YT-1300 light freighter]] [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], operated by Calrissian and Kaeg and a [[Miy'tari Scout]] piloted by [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] [[Ben Skywalker]] and [[Tahiri Veila]], into [[Ambush at Ohali Soroc's supposed crash site|an ambush]] by broadcasting a false RiftMesh distress call, supposedly from [[Incom reconnaissance craft X396|the starfighter]] of the missing [[Quest Knights|Quest Knight]] [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Ohali Soroc]].<ref name="Crucible" />
 
==Behind the scenes==
The RiftMesh featured in the [[2013]] [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] novel [[Crucible (novel)|''Crucible'']], written by [[Troy Denning]].<ref name="Crucible" />
